value: Which shop do you mean by "the actual shop"? I have the comparison ready for all 57 of them but cannot hand you one figure, because the answer swings between 0.16x and 2.32x depending on which shop you meant. (1) ONE SPECIFIC SHOP — name it and you get one number. The list runs: Contoso Store New Brunswick and Contoso Store North Dakota, both 3500 m², 2.3152x; South Australia 3000 m², 1.9844x; Mecklenburg-Vorpommern 2800 m², 1.8522x; Newfoundland and Labrador 2105 m², 1.3924x; Ayrshire, Blaenau Gwent and Pesaro all 2100 m², 1.3891x; down to Contoso Store Corse, 245 m², 0.1621x. The middle shop is 0.9922x — dead average. Only 18 of the 57 are within a quarter of average, and it is nearly a coin flip whether yours is above (28 shops) or below (29), so guessing would not serve you. (2) EVERY SHOP, ONE RATIO EACH — already computed: 57 rows, 2.3152x down to 0.1621x. Say the word and this is your answer. (3) ALL SHOPS ADDED TOGETHER against the average — exactly 57.00, since total floor area over average floor area can only ever be the shop count; almost certainly not what you meant. WHAT YOUR CHOICE DOES NOT CHANGE: the average, 1511.75 m² over all 57 trading shops. It is the same denominator under all three readings, and even widening the population to include the 16 closed shops moves it only to 1494.79 m² — about 1%, too small to move any shop across the average line except one sitting right on it.

The 57 physical shops with no close date — every figure I quote (the 1511.7544 m² average, the 2.3152x–0.1621x span, the 0.9922x median, the 28-above/29-below split, the 18-within-a-quarter count) is computed over exactly those 57 rows and nothing wider. Two restrictions, both taken from declared defaults rather than from the question: PHYSICAL ONLY (location_code <> -1) per store.resolution.the_channel_is_the_location_sentinel, whose `default: physical` carries `applies: subject` and the subject here is a Store — and in any case the online row's square_metres is NULL, so it cannot enter a size average under any reading; and STILL TRADING (close_date IS NULL) per store.resolution.active_is_the_absent_close_date, `default: active`, because the question named no trading state. The 16 closed or restructured shops sit outside both the candidate list and the average. No period restriction and none meaningful: floor area is a standing attribute declared a STOCK, not a figure accumulated over a window. Grain is PREMISES, which over this population coincides exactly with sites — 57 shops over 57 distinct location codes — so no re-let site is double-counted.

WITH shops AS (
  SELECT
    store_name,
    square_metres
  FROM contoso_served.dim_store
  WHERE
    location_code <> -1 AND close_date IS NULL
), avg_m2 AS (
  SELECT
    AVG(square_metres) AS a,
    COUNT(*) AS n,
    SUM(square_metres) AS s
  FROM shops
)
SELECT
  'smallest shop' AS reading,
  s.store_name,
  s.square_metres AS shop_m2,
  ROUND(a.a, 2) AS avg_m2,
  ROUND(s.square_metres / a.a, 4) AS ratio
FROM shops AS s, avg_m2 AS a
WHERE
  s.square_metres = (
    SELECT
      MIN(square_metres)
    FROM shops
  )
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'largest shop',
  s.store_name,
  s.square_metres,
  ROUND(a.a, 2),
  ROUND(s.square_metres / a.a, 4)
FROM shops AS s, avg_m2 AS a
WHERE
  s.square_metres = (
    SELECT
      MAX(square_metres)
    FROM shops
  )
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'all 57 shops added together',
  'all shops',
  a.s,
  ROUND(a.a, 2),
  ROUND(a.s / a.a, 4)
FROM avg_m2 AS a
ORDER BY
  ratio

    store_name,
    square_metres
  FROM contoso_served.dim_store

  s.square_metres AS shop_m2,

FROM shops AS s, avg_m2 AS a
ORDER BY
  ratio_to_average DESC,
  s.store_name

WITH shops AS (
  SELECT
    store_name,
    square_metres
  FROM contoso_served.dim_store
  WHERE
    location_code <> -1 AND close_date IS NULL
), avg_m2 AS (
  SELECT
    AVG(square_metres) AS a
  FROM shops
), r AS (
  SELECT
    s.store_name,
    s.square_metres,
    s.square_metres / a.a AS ratio
  FROM shops AS s, avg_m2 AS a
)
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS candidate_shops,
  ROUND(MIN(ratio), 4) AS lowest_ratio,
  ROUND(MAX(ratio), 4) AS highest_ratio,
  ROUND(MEDIAN(ratio), 4) AS median_ratio,
  SUM(CASE WHEN ratio > 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS above_average,
  SUM(CASE WHEN ratio < 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS below_average,
  SUM(CASE WHEN ratio BETWEEN 0.8 AND 1.25 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS within_a_quarter_of_average,
  SUM(CASE WHEN ratio >= 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS at_least_twice_average
FROM r
